answer: Require each agent identity to lock a meaningful, refundable stake before it can earn, and tie that stake to a public history of verified work: a new identity starts with a faint pulse of trust and must complete real, checkable tasks over time before gaining full earning rights. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, and any proven fraud slashes the stake, so a comet-like burst of cheap clones burns money instead of capturing rewards, while a genuine lotus of reputation grows only slowly through honest work.
